title: What happened
goal: Talk about past events: where you went, what you did, what happened — using the ergative construction correctly.
intro:
The Gujarati past tense has two patterns. With verbs that have **no object** (go, come, sit), the past works like an adjective agreeing with the subject: **હું ગયો** 'I went' (man), **હું ગઈ** (woman).

With verbs that **take an object** (eat, see, say), Gujarati uses the **ergative construction**: the doer gets the ending **-એ** (or a special pronoun form like **મેં** 'I'), and the verb agrees with the **object**, not the doer: **મેં ચા પીધી** 'I drank tea' — પીધી is feminine because ચા is feminine.

ગયા અઠવાડિયે 'last week', ગયા વર્ષે 'last year'

grammar.title: Past tense of intransitive verbs: agree with the subject
grammar.body:
The past form is made from the stem + **-યો / -ી / -યું / -યા / -યાં** (like an adjective). With verbs that take no object, it agrees with the **subject**:

હું આવ**્યો** (man) / આવ**ી** (woman) — I came
એ આવ**્યો** / આવ**ી** — he / she came
અમે આવ**્યા** (men or mixed) / આવ**્યાં** (mixed or neuter) — we came
બાળક આવ**્યું** — the child came

Important irregulars: **જવું → ગયો / ગઈ / ગયું**, **થવું → થયો / થઈ / થયું**, **બેસવું → બેઠો**, **સૂવું → સૂતો**, **રહેવું → રહ્યો**.

Negative: add **નહીં** after or **નથી** before: **એ આવ્યો નહીં** / **એ નથી આવ્યો** 'he didn't come / hasn't come'.

grammar.title: The ergative: મેં ચા પીધી
grammar.body:
With **transitive** verbs (verbs with an object), the past tense uses the ergative construction:

1. The **doer takes -એ**: રામ → **રામે**, સીતા → **સીતાએ**, છોકરો → **છોકરાએ**. Pronouns: **મેં** (I), **તેં** (you, intimate), **એણે / તેણે** (he, she), **અમે / આપણે** (we), **તમે** (you), **એમણે / તેમણે** (they; he/she respectful).
2. The **verb agrees with the object**: ચા (f) → **પીધી**; પાણી (n) → **પીધું**; નાસ્તો (m) → **કર્યો**; રોટલી (f pl) → **ખાધી**.

So **મેં ચા પીધી**, **મેં પાણી પીધું**, **સીતાએ નાસ્તો કર્યો** — the verb doesn't care whether the doer is male or female. Unlike Hindi (where a को-marked object leaves the verb in the default masculine), standard Gujarati keeps this agreement even when the object is marked with -ને: **મેં સીતાને જોઈ** 'I saw Sita' (જોઈ is feminine because Sita is), **સીતાએ રમેશને જોયો** 'Sita saw Ramesh' (masculine, agreeing with Ramesh), **એણે મને બોલાવી** 'he called me' (said by a woman). With no clear object, use neuter -યું: **તમે શું કહ્યું?**

Key irregular pasts: **ખાવું → ખાધું, પીવું → પીધું, લેવું → લીધું, દેવું → દીધું, કરવું → કર્યું, કહેવું → કહ્યું, જોવું → જોયું**.

examples.en: Sita wrote a letter. (પત્ર is m)
We bought a new house. (ઘર is n)
Did you see Sita? (intimate; જોઈ agrees with Sita, f)
What did they / did he (resp.) say?

grammar.title: Perfect and past continuous: છે, હતું, -તો હતો
grammar.body:
Add **છે** to the past form for the present perfect ('have done'): **હું આવ્યો છું** 'I have come', **મેં ખાધું છે** 'I have eaten'.

Add **હતું** (agreeing) for the pluperfect or a completed past: **અમે કચ્છ ગયાં હતાં** 'we had gone / went to Kutch'.

For 'was doing' or 'used to do', use the **-તો** form + **હતો**: **હું વાંચતો હતો** 'I was reading / used to read'. Without હતો, the bare -તો form also means 'used to' in storytelling: **અમે રોજ દરિયે જતા** 'we used to go to the sea every day'.

examples.native: જ્યારે ફોન આવ્યો, હું જમતો હતો.
examples.roman: jyāre fon āvyo, huṃ jamto hato.
examples.en: When the phone rang, I was eating.
As a child I used to play cricket.

dialogue.title: Monday morning
dialogue.setting: Colleagues Bhavin and Sarah catch up about the weekend.

lines.speaker: Bhavin
lines.en: Sarah, what did you do at the weekend?

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.native: શનિવારે હું મારી બહેનપણીના લગ્નમાં ગઈ.
lines.roman: shanivāre huṃ mārī bahenpaṇīnā lagnamāṃ gaī.
lines.en: On Saturday I went to my friend's wedding.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.native: બહુ મજા આવી. હું પહેલી વાર ગરબા રમી!
lines.roman: bahu majā āvī. huṃ pahelī vār garbā ramī!
lines.en: It was great fun. I danced garba for the first time!

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.native: રવિવારે હું આખો દિવસ સૂતી રહી. તમે શું કર્યું?
lines.roman: ravivāre huṃ ākho divas sūtī rahī. tame shuṃ karyuṃ?
lines.en: On Sunday I slept all day. What did you do?

lines.speaker: Bhavin
lines.native: અમે મૅચ જોઈ. પણ ભારત હારી ગયું.
lines.roman: ame mech joī. paṇ Bhārat hārī gayuṃ.
lines.en: We watched the match. But India lost.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.en: Oh no! I haven't seen the news.

lines.speaker: Bhavin
lines.native: કોઈ વાંધો નહીં. આવતી વખતે જીતીશું!
lines.roman: koī vāṃdho nahīṃ. āvtī vakhate jītīshuṃ!
lines.en: Never mind. We'll win next time!

culture: **તમે જમ્યા?** 'Have you eaten?' is as much a greeting of care as a real question in Gujarati homes. Gujarati weddings last several days, with a **ગરબા/દાંડિયા** night, **મહેંદી**, and the ceremony itself; guests are fed generously and gifts of cash (**ચાંલ્લો** *chāṃllo*) in round-plus-one amounts (₹501, ₹1101) are customary.

tip.title: Past tense: 'went', 'came', 'broke'
tip.body:
- Verbs with no object agree with the **subject** in the past: હું આવ**્યો** (man), હું આવ**ી** (woman), અમે આવ**્યા**, બાળક આવ**્યું**.
- Irregular: જવું → **ગયો / ગઈ / ગયું**, થવું → **થયો / થઈ / થયું**.
- **… ગયો** after a stem in -ઈ means it happened completely: ફોન **તૂટી ગયો**.

sentences.en: My brother went to the office in the morning.
The kids went out to play.

lessons.title: Last week, last year

tip.title: 'Last week', 'once', 'back'
tip.body:
- 'Last' is **ગયા** with the time word in its -એ form: **ગયા અઠવાડિયે**, **ગયા મહિને**, **ગયા વર્ષે**.
- **વાર** 'time' is feminine: **એક વાર** 'once', **પહેલી વાર** 'the first time', **ઘણી વાર** 'often'.
- **પાછું** 'back' agrees: એ **પાછો** આવ્યો, એ **પાછી** આવી, પપ્પા **પાછા** આવ્યા.
tip.pattern: ગયા + મહિને / વર્ષે · પાછો / પાછી આવ્યો

new: ગયા વર્ષે અમે કચ્છ ગયાં હતાં.

sentences.en: Last week I went to Mumbai. (man)
Last month we went on a trip.

sentences.en: It's my first time in India. (woman)

sentences.en: Dad came back from the office.

sentences.roman: huṃ ek vār Kachchh gaī chhuṃ.

sentences.native: ગયા મહિને દાદા સાથે મુલાકાત થઈ.
sentences.roman: gayā mahine dādā sāthe mulākāt thaī.

tip.title: મેં … — 'I did' with an object
tip.body:
- With a verb that has an object, the doer takes **-એ**: **મેં** (I), **એણે** (he/she), **તેં** (you, friend), **માએ** (Mum); **અમે, તમે** don't change.
- The verb agrees with the **object**: મેં ચા **પીધી** (f), મેં પાણી **પીધું** (n), મેં નાસ્તો **કર્યો** (m).
- No clear object → **-યું**: તમે શું **કહ્યું**?
tip.pattern: મેં + object + verb (agreeing with the object)

sentences.en: Did you send me the photos?
Yesterday we saw the new film.
I had two chapatis in the morning.
Have you had breakfast? (to a friend)

tip.title: Winning, losing, celebrating
tip.body:
- **જીતવું** takes an object, so it's ergative: **ભારતે** મૅચ **જીતી** (મૅચ is f).
- **હારવું** usually has no object: આપણે **હારી ગયા**.
- **મળવું** 'to get' and 'to meet' are not ergative: મને ભેટ **મળી** 'I got a present', હું મિત્રને **મળ્યો** 'I met a friend'.
- Celebrating: અમે જન્મદિવસ **ઉજવ્યો** (m).
tip.pattern: ભારતે મૅચ જીતી · મને ભેટ મળી

sentences.native: ગયા રવિવારે મેં મારો જન્મદિવસ ઉજવ્યો.
sentences.roman: gayā ravivāre meṃ māro janmdivas ujavyo.
sentences.en: Last Sunday I celebrated my birthday.
I gave her a nice present.
I got your present, thank you!

sentences.native: હું ગઈકાલે મારા જૂના મિત્રને મળ્યો.
sentences.roman: huṃ gaīkāle mārā jūnā mitrane maḷyo.
sentences.en: I met an old friend yesterday. (man)

sentences.native: મારા ભાઈનાં લગ્ન ગયા મહિને થયાં.
sentences.roman: mārā bhāīnāṃ lagna gayā mahine thayāṃ.
sentences.en: My brother got married last month.
What time did the match start?

tip.title: Have done, had done, was doing
tip.body:
- **છે** after the past form = 'have done': તમે કચ્છ જોયું **છે**? Negative: મેં **નથી** જોયું.
- **હતું** (agreeing) after it = 'had done' or a finished past: આપણે અહીં આવ્યા **હતા**.
- 'Was doing': the **-તો** form + **હતો**: હું વાંચ**તો હતો**.

sentences.native: તમને યાદ છે? ગયા વર્ષે આપણે અહીં આવ્યા હતા.
sentences.roman: tamne yād chhe? gayā varṣe āpaṇe ahīṃ āvyā hatā.
sentences.en: Do you remember? We came here last year.

sentences.native: ગઈકાલે સાંજે હું ચોપડી વાંચતો હતો.
sentences.roman: gaīkāle sāṃje huṃ chopḍī vāṃchto hato.
sentences.en: Yesterday evening I was reading a book. (man)
